title: The Future XI: Designing Lucknow Super Giants’s Ideal Role Balance, Not a Dream Team
dek: A dream team picks the best eleven names. A future XI starts from roles: how many bowlers a side really uses, how deep the batting goes, and how much spin the plan needs.
excerpt: Since 2022, Lucknow Super Giants have used a measurable number of bowlers and batters per innings and a spin share that can be set against the league. Those numbers define the roles a future XI has to fill.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Roles Before Names
body: A future XI should be designed as a set of roles: how many genuine bowling options, how deep the batting must go, and the balance of pace and spin. Names follow from the roles.
Since 2022, Lucknow Super Giants have used {{ev:fx-bm}} bowlers per innings, against {{ev:fx-bo}} for the rest of the IPL. The chart tracks it by season.

sections.heading: Batting Depth and Spin
body: LSG have used {{ev:fx-tm}} batters per innings, against {{ev:fx-to}} across the league, a measure of how often the lower order is needed.
Spin has bowled {{ev:fx-sm}} of their overs, against {{ev:fx-so}} for the league.

sections.heading: Proposal: A Role Template
body: Proposal: design the future XI as six batting roles (two openers, an anchor, two middle-order hitters and a finisher), five bowling roles split by phase, and one impact-player slot reserved for the matchup of the day.

sections.heading: Limits
body: Bowling style is known for most but not all bowlers. Counts of bowlers and batters used reflect match situations as well as plans: a collapse uses more batters whatever the design.
The impact-player rule makes any fixed XI less fixed than it used to be.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Build the Roles, Then Fill Them
body: Lucknow Super Giants should define the roles their XI needs from how they actually play, then use the auction and academy to fill them.
That is the difference between a future XI and a dream team.
